note: Both semantic backends are unreachable in this container — fastembed's weights come from huggingface.co and the ollama backend needs a daemon from ollama.com, and egress policy refuses both. The semantic seam was therefore the one part of the product that could not be exercised at all. A small model was stood up as a recallable scoring service in its place, which made the seam measurable and then produced a result about itself that the first measurement got wrong. Recorded in IDEAS 6.99.

decisions.question: The semantic seam cannot run in this box at all. Leave it unmeasured, or stand up a language model as a stand-in for the embedder?
decisions.commitment: Stand one up, and make it recallable so it can be called repeatedly with one protocol rather than re-specified per call. It answers the score(raw_a, raw_b) half of the Matcher seam directly rather than producing vectors — a scoring service, not an embedding backend.
decisions.why: An unexercised seam is where a defect can sit indefinitely, and the two things a semantic matcher is supposed to buy were both unmeasurable: retrieval that character ratio cannot reach, and separation of names that look alike. The stand-in put numbers on both in one pass — 0.098 to 0.900 on a name against its own description, 0.741 down to 0.600 on two look-alike repo names. Neither number existed before, and neither needed the blocked hosts to obtain.

decisions.question: The stand-in re-scored four pairs and reproduced all four exactly, note strings included. Record that as determinism?
decisions.commitment: No. Ran a fresh-context control with the identical protocol, and every non-identical pair moved — mean absolute drift 0.050, max 0.075, all four downward. The first agent had been resumed from its own transcript and could read its previous answers, so the reproduction was recall rather than a stable function.
decisions.why: Exact reproduction including free-text notes is the tell: a function that scores meaning has no reason to phrase its explanation identically twice. The control is what distinguishes a stable instrument from one that remembers, and there is no way to tell those apart from inside a single conversation. The same failure would have been invisible if the stand-in had only ever been called the way it was designed to be called.

decisions.question: The stand-in broke an explicit rule in its own rubric — look-alike names denoting different things were told to score <=0.35 and came back 0.500 and 0.600. Agent drift, or a defect in the instructions?
decisions.commitment: A defect in the instructions. The rubric also carried a 0.500 anchor for 'same domain or family, different subject', which those pairs satisfy equally, so two clauses both applied and the agent resolved them the same way both times. The fresh control reproduced the violation independently, which is what settles it.
decisions.why: Worth recording because the reflex is to read a broken rule as the model being unreliable, and that reading would have been wrong here and would have led to tightening the wrong thing. A rule reproduced identically by an instance that never saw the first one is a property of the prompt. It is the same distinction the store makes everywhere else: what an instrument reports about itself is not evidence until something independent produces it too.

decisions.question: What is this stand-in allowed to be used for?
decisions.commitment: A measuring instrument, not a backend. It may put numbers on what the semantic seam would buy; it may not key the embedding cache and it may not stand behind a seal. embedding_store.py keys vectors by model_name, and that key is a promise the function behind it is fixed — which this one demonstrably is not.
decisions.why: The drift observed is far below the shipped 0.92 threshold, so nothing in this sample flips served against not-served, and it would be easy to conclude the instability does not matter. It matters at the cache, not at the threshold: a cache hit and a fresh call returning different numbers makes the stored row unreproducible, which is the property the whole store is built to protect. Naming the permitted use now is cheaper than discovering the boundary later through a cached row nobody can regenerate.
